selected_primary_idea.title: Braiding-Readiness Evidence Ledger (BREL)
selected_primary_idea.one_sentence: Replace the single-signature search with a pre-registered multi-axis realization witness that links phase identification, nonlocality, fusion/exchange order dependence, protection scaling, and a universality budget to device-level falsification controls.
selected_primary_idea.scientific_object: A gate-defined network of semiconductor-superconductor islands intended as a future Majorana-qubit primitive.
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: If a controllable topological Majorana sector is present, then a linked sequence of tests will jointly show a reproducible gapped regime, nonlocal parity structure, protocol-order-dependent fusion/exchange outcomes, and improved protected-error proxies with separation/temperature/time under predeclared null controls; a local trivial model will fail at least one independent axis.
falsification_conditions: A deliberately trivial or scrambled control matches the full multi-axis signature within the predeclared uncertainty bounds.
Changing exchange order has no result distinguishable from a control protocol after correcting for readout bias and drift.
The claimed nonlocal signal remains unchanged when the remote segment is detuned or when a local model predicts otherwise.
Protection proxies do not improve with the separated-encoding design variables, or their trend is explained by an ordinary local control effect.
The architecture lacks a quantified route from protected Clifford operations to a non-Clifford resource.
selected_primary_idea.expected_contribution: A sharper experimental decision rule: classify a platform as phase candidate, nonlocal candidate, braiding-ready primitive, or not supported, rather than using an unqualified positive/negative Majorana label.
